t: Germany went for Stalingrad as part of a summer offensive aimed at the Caucasus oil fields, and the city became a matter of prestige for both Hitler and Stalin.
After three months of house-to-house fighting in which the Germans took 90% of the ruined city, the Red Army encircled the 6th Army from its flanks on 19 to 23 November 1942.
Casualty figures are widely disputed, with Axis estimates from 800,000 to 1,500,000 and Soviet archival totals of over a million, and most German prisoners died in captivity.
dyk: Between 23 and 26 August 1942 Soviet reports record 955 people killed and 1,181 wounded in the bombing, while estimates of civilian dead from the bombing reach 40,000 or 70,000, though these may be exaggerated.
ev: Case Blue, the German summer offensive, opens on 28 June
German forces first clash with the Stalingrad Front on 17 July in the bend of the Don
The 6th Army reaches the outskirts on 23 August and Luftflotte 4 bombs the city
The battle for the city itself begins on 13 September
On 14 October a German assault reaches the Volga at the tractor factory and splits the 62nd Army
Operation Uranus opens on 19 November and the ring closes at Kalach on 23 November
Operation Winter Storm, the German relief attempt, is abandoned on 23 December
The southern pocket collapses on 31 January and the northern pocket surrenders on 2 February

f.date: 17 July 1942 (first clash on the approaches) to 2 February 1943; the German offensive on the city began on 23 August 1942
f.place: The city of Stalingrad (now Volgograd) on the Volga and the steppe around it, in southern Russia
f.sides: The Soviet Union (five armies in and around the city, under commanders including Chuikov and Yeryomenko, with nine more in the counteroffensive) against Germany and its Axis allies: the 6th Army under Paulus and the 4th Panzer Army under Hoth of Army Group B under Weichs, with Romanian, Italian, Hungarian and Croatian forces; about 330,000 Axis personnel were encircled
f.outcome: The Soviet counteroffensive encircled the German 6th Army, which surrendered on 2 February 1943 with around 91,000 prisoners taken.
